text:
ajay: Heads-up — saw a prefill + demote interleaving that caused a double-apply and stale-read from the kvcache canary. repro logs below, low-noise but reproducible under churn.

ajay: repro steps I used: create tenant with hot prefixes, force prefix prefill, concurrently trigger demote on same prefix, then read. Observed prefill apply after demote with older state.
```
2026-03-20T10:12:02.123Z INFO prefill start prefix=tenant-42/0 prefetch_id=pf_9 lease=8273 epoch=12
2026-03-20T10:12:02.125Z INFO demote begin prefix=tenant-42/0 lease=8273 epoch=13
2026-03-20T10:12:02.128Z INFO demote complete prefix=tenant-42/0 lease=8273 epoch=13
2026-03-20T10:12:02.130Z INFO prefill apply prefix=tenant-42/0 prefetch_id=pf_9 lease=8273 epoch=12 applied=true
2026-03-20T10:12:02.131Z WARN  client-read prefix=tenant-42/0 saw_stale=true
```

maria: ugh, that looks like prefill doesn't check current lease/epoch before applying. can you dump the lease object fields? suspect inflight-flag isn't enough.

ajay: lease object dump shows: lease=8273 { epoch:13, holder:node-5, revoked:false } but prefill still applied because it only checked lease id equality, not epoch.

lucas: this is similar to the old handoff epoch idea. If we carry a prefix_epoch with the prefill and compare on apply, we can ignore stale prefills. cheap compare.

tanya: adding a per-prefill epoch check is nice, but do we pay on every lookup? or only on apply? We only need to check during apply (prefill -> writeback) so per-apply cost is negligible.

maria: alternative: attach a revocation hook to the lease so demote calls into any inflight prefill to cancel. avoids adding metadata to every prefill. downside: cross-shard callback complexity.

ajay: callback introduces locking and ordering complexity across shards. during demote we might already be holding shard locks; invoking callbacks risks lock inversion. epoch compare is simpler and makes apply idempotent.

lucas: propose POC: add prefix_epoch:u64 to Prefill metadata, and have Prefill.apply() compare current lease. If prefill.epoch != lease.epoch drop and emit metric prefills.dropped_stale. Low-risk and reversible.

tanya: +1. make sure to increment epoch on demote and handoff paths that change ownership. Also add loadtest with demote churn to ensure we don't regress latency.

ajay: can we also add a small trace/span tag pref_epoch so postmortems show it (helpful for verifying)?

lucas: yes, add trace set_preload_epoch and trace check_prefill_epoch.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary kvcache-prefill-epoch-probe -> us-west1 (3 nodes) at 2026-03-20T10:15Z :rocket:

maria: I'll run smoke tests on canary tonight. quick test plan: 1) create tenant w/ hot keys 2) spawn concurrent prefill + demote loops 3) assert no double-apply metrics and no stale reads 4) collect traces.

ajay: if POC passes we should RFC minimal API change: Prefill { epoch: u64 } and Lease { epoch: u64 } + apply-time check. Keep upgrade path: ignore missing epoch (old nodes) for a while.

lucas: also update per-prefix eviction doc: demote->evict ordering still a separate concern. this only prevents stale prefills from resurfacing old data after a demote. file a follow-up.

tanya: I'll draft small perf microbenchmark for the apply path overhead. likely <1% but need numbers.

ajay: created issue RR-4121 with logs and proposed patch sketch: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/RR-4121

maria: assigned POC to self. will ping #eng-runtime with results and metrics. :thumbsup:
